parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. The division itself is protective and documented as operating: a 2014 public-accommodations law covering gender identity, hate-crime penalties since 2021, abolished gay/trans panic defence, a 2024 signed sanctuary law, marker changes and X on state IDs, plus placement among the safest bands on law score and recorded incidents. But the parent's regime governs every border and federal touchpoint: X-marker elimination, M/F-only processing, a cable instructing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex (with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility), federal facility exclusion by birth sex, documented immigration-detention abuse, and a 2026 federal corrections conversion-therapy mandate. State protections cannot cancel federal entry screening or federal custody. Public opinion (66% backing birth-sex documents) raises outing friction. Net: everyday acceptance inside the state, but genuine federal exposures at entry and if detained.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order ended X markers and requires M/F per assigned-sex documents; Nov 2025 court allowed it. Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated abroad; eight governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Division issues X on licences and voter registration since 2019 and allows birth-certificate marker change since 2015; pre-existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Legal-aid FAQ guides document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport governs entry, but the federal cable and screening apply at the US border regardless of division law; state ID cannot cure a border discrepancy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration-detention abuse of transgender men: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse. From 2026 federal corrections mandates conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs) and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division hate-crime statute (2021) and 2014 nondiscrimination law; state law enforcement subject to these. State custody placement rules for trans people: not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal immigration custody and federal prisons sit entirely outside division protection; the sanctuary law's coverage of non-resident visitors is not sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; 4 states criminalise certain restroom use (one trespass arrest of a trans woman, held 24h in a men's ward); a Feb 2026 state law invalidating non-matching documents is called a template.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no facilities ban; 2014 public-accommodations law protects access, a 2018 national ruling backs trans students, counties/cities provide gender-neutral options.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal building/airport exclusion still operates inside the division, so the traveller loses protection exactly at federally controlled sites.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders freeze funding, label youth care 'mutilation', propose barring insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s; 27 states ban youth gender care; specialised LGBTQ crisis services shut in 2025.
care_services.protection: Division covers gender-affirming care in public insurance for residents 18+, has the country's most trans-friendly insurance law, a 2023 protective executive order, and bans conversion therapy on minors since 2018.
care_services.interaction: Resident coverage does not extend to visitors; the traveller depends on own insurance or out-of-pocket, and federal rule proposals could affect federally funded settings.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; Dec 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; DOJ directed to investigate schools; 2025 poll: 66% back birth-sex documents, 69% backing sports bans.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division created an LGBTIQ+ affairs commission (2021, expanded 2023), passed sanctuary status 2024, and abolished the gay/trans panic defence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises outing probability and official scrutiny at airports, federal buildings and border interviews, where division policy does not reach.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; youth care banned in 27 states; federal facility rules apply to schools and federally funded sites.
minors_guardians.protection: Division bans youth conversion therapy, permits trans athletes per identity in a county report, and protects gender identity in public accommodations; schools there are not subject to a division ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor still faces federal document and entry screening; whether sanctuary or division protections reach a visiting family is not sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two Black trans women shot dead in the largest city within ten weeks by Sept 2026, perpetrator at large; no general homicide rate supplied, so magnitude versus background is unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division listed among safest on law score and recorded incidents; gender-identity hate-crime penalties since 2021; statewide nondiscrimination enforcement machinery exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: None documented between division policing practice and federal agencies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal orders partly enjoined and litigation unresolved, so exposure shifts with travel date; state custody placement, per-capita violence denominators, and sanctuary coverage of visitors are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit against passport policy, legal-aid FAQ, working state nondiscrimination and hate-crime remedies, and the July 2026 analysis placing the division in its safest band.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies cannot reverse a border refusal, a fraud finding, or federal detention abuse; oversight there does operate for division-level discrimination.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's routine, universal exclusion register with no remedy is harsher: exclusion is near-automatic and unappealable. Here refusal is contingent on a document discrepancy, litigation is live, and the division offers strong internal protections. Border exclusion risk is real but narrower, so materially higher than 0.35.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening with administrative refusal, slow remedies and humiliation — close to this dossier's federal border posture. This case is lower on some axes (documented detention abuse, federal facility bans) but higher on others (functioning state nondiscrimination, hate-crime and sanctuary machinery, safest-band incident record), roughly netting to this level.

Meridia's trained border officers, brief detention with counsel, written reasons and compensation describes the division's internal posture fairly well, but not the federal layer: lifetime fraud exposure, X-marker elimination and custody abuse push the combined regime a clear step below 0.75.

Vellmaris: brief stop for document mismatch, national protection, working complaint remedy with apology. The division resembles this, but the parent's nationwide marker regime and detention record are more adverse than Vellmaris's provincial ordinance, so slightly lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes in sequence. At the border and in federally controlled spaces the parent's hostile machinery governs: X-marker elimination, refusal on document discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud findings, facility exclusion by birth sex, and — if detained — documented immigration-detention abuse and a 2026 conversion-therapy corrections policy. Inside the division, documented and operating protections (public accommodations since 2014, hate-crime penalties, sanctuary law, marker changes, gender-neutral facilities, low recorded incidents, an active commission) make everyday life closer to a Reduced-Risk jurisdiction, tempered by two recent killings with unknown background rate and a public opinion climate favouring birth-sex documents. Because federal exposures attach at entry and custody — stages every visitor passes through or may enter — the combined score sits mid-scale rather than with the division's protective band.
